attempts.sql: WITH connector_classes AS (SELECT c.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, c.file_id, c.qualname, c.name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS c JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb ON cb.class_symbol_id = c.symbol_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND cb.base_symbol_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py::SQLDatabase' AND NOT (c.file_id LIKE 'tests/%' OR c.file_id LIKE '%/tests/%')), sqldb_methods AS (SELECT m.name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS m WHERE m.file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname = 'SQLDatabase.' || m.name) SELECT DISTINCT cc.class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM connector_classes AS cc JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS m ON m.file_id = cc.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname = cc.qualname || '.' || m.name WHERE m.is_public = TRUE AND SUBSTR(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sqldb_methods AS sm WHERE sm.name = m.name) ORDER BY cc.class_symbol_id, method_name;

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
Return exactly the requested output columns, using each requested name as the column alias, in the requested order. Return complete repository-relative file paths and complete symbol IDs exactly as stored. When the question asks which files, symbols or modules, return each distinct one once unless it asks for occurrences.
explanation: This query lists the public methods that each production database connector class defines in its own body but that SQLDatabase does not define. It uses the symbols and class bases tables to identify direct subclasses of SQLDatabase, excludes any class whose file path is under a tests folder, and filters to methods whose names do not start with an underscore. The results are returned as distinct pairs of class symbol ID and method name, ordered by class symbol ID and method name.
sql: WITH connector_classes AS (SELECT c.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, c.file_id, c.qualname, c.name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS c JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb ON cb.class_symbol_id = c.symbol_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND cb.base_symbol_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py::SQLDatabase' AND NOT (c.file_id LIKE 'tests/%' OR c.file_id LIKE '%/tests/%')), sqldb_methods AS (SELECT m.name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS m WHERE m.file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname = 'SQLDatabase.' || m.name) SELECT DISTINCT cc.class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM connector_classes AS cc JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS m ON m.file_id = cc.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname = cc.qualname || '.' || m.name WHERE m.is_public = TRUE AND SUBSTR(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sqldb_methods AS sm WHERE sm.name = m.name) ORDER BY cc.class_symbol_id, method_name;
